Properties may also be eligible under this criterion if they represent a significant and distinguishable entity whose components may lack individual distinction. The Technical Support Building is one in a number of large, pre-cast concrete buildings in the Area 6 Control Point and helps to convey the district’s overall utilitarian, military-industrial character. While it has some minor variation with the 240-foot-long loading dock and electrical power hookups for trailers, it is not architecturally significant or unique, nor does it represent the work of a master. It does not possess high artistic value, nor is it a significant and distinguishable entity in its own right. Building 06-CP-65 is not recommended eligible under Criterion C. Criterion D. Properties significant under Criterion D must have the potential to yield further information about human history that can only be answered by the actual physical material of the resources. There are two requirements for a resource to be found significant under Criterion D: the property must have or have had information to contribute to our understanding of human history or prehistory, and the information must be considered important. The Technical Support Building has been subject to research on its role in nuclear testing on the NNSS. It is unlikely that the building itself could yield more information that would be considered important. Building 06-CP-65 does not appear to be significant under Criterion D. The building is still being used for storage and remains in its original location, retaining its original materials, design, and workmanship. It has lost some degree of integrity of setting, association, and feeling because the Area 6 Control Point Historic District is no longer used by the NNSS for aiding nuclear weapons testing, the buildings in the Control Point have almost all been abandoned, and some have been demolished since the end of nuclear testing in 1992. 7. Narrative Architectural Description Provide a detailed description of the resource, including all character defining features, potential construction methods, potential alterations (both historic and non-historic), and any accessory resources. The Technical Support Building or 06-CP-65 was constructed in 1966 as a large warehouse for equipment used in the forward areas of the NNSS. It also was used as office space for engineers, administrative functions and records, and laboratories. It is a concrete building located in the Area 6 Control Point just west of Mercury Highway. It is one- story, has a 240 × 100 ft. rectangular plan that is oriented north-south, and is made with precast concrete wall panels. A loading dock with electrical power hook-ups runs the length of the east elevation with concrete stairs located at both ends. The high, built-up roof sits on concrete and metal decking and is nearly flat with a very low pitch to accommodate proper drainage.
